description: A comprehensive study of the behavior of solid bodies under external loads, focusing on their internal resisting forces, deformations, and the governing theories of failure.

sections.title: Simple Stress and Strain
sections.description: Fundamental behavior of materials under axial loading and the mathematical relationships between various elastic constants.

equations: Hooke's Law: Stress = E * Strain (valid only within the proportional limit)
Elastic Constants Relations: E = 2G(1 + mu) = 3K(1 - 2mu) = (9KG) / (3K + G)

key_concepts.explanation: The absolute ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain within the elastic limit. For most structural engineering materials, its value lies between 0 and 0.5.

Stress induced in a body when it is subjected to a change in temperature and its natural volumetric expansion or contraction is either entirely or partially prevented by rigid supports. Stress = alpha * T * E.

sections.title: Shear Force and Bending Moment Diagrams (SFD & BMD)
sections.description: Graphical representations showing the variation of internal shear forces and bending moments along the length of a beam subjected to transverse loading.

key_concepts.explanation: The specific point on a Bending Moment Diagram (BMD) where the bending moment changes sign (transitions from positive/sagging to negative/hogging, or vice versa), indicating that the bending moment is exactly zero at this location.

results: The maximum or minimum bending moment in a beam occurs exactly at the cross-section where the shear force is either zero or changes its sign.
If a section of the beam is subjected to a Uniformly Distributed Load (UDL), the SFD will be an inclined straight line (1st degree), and the BMD will be a parabolic curve (2nd degree).

sections.title: Bending and Shear Stresses in Beams
sections.description: Calculation of internal stresses induced across the cross-section of a flexural member due to pure bending moments and transverse shear forces.

equations: M / I = sigma / y = E / R
Where M is Bending Moment, I is Area Moment of Inertia, sigma is Bending Stress, and R is the Radius of Curvature.

cases.condition: Maximum Transverse Shear Stress in Standard Cross-sections
results: Rectangular Cross-section: Max Shear Stress = 1.5 * Average Shear Stress (occurs at the neutral axis).
Solid Circular Cross-section: Max Shear Stress = 1.33 * Average Shear Stress (4/3 * Average, occurs at the neutral axis).
Triangular Cross-section: Max Shear Stress = 1.5 * Average Shear Stress (occurs at h/2 height, not at the neutral axis which is at h/3).

sections.title: Torsion of Circular Shafts
sections.description: Analysis of solid and hollow circular shafts subjected to twisting moments (torque), focusing on shear stress distribution and angular deformations.

equations: T / J = tau / R = G * theta / L
Where T is Torque, J is Polar Moment of Inertia, tau is Maximum Shear Stress, and theta is the Angle of Twist.

formulas.category: Power Transmitted by a Rotating Shaft
equations: Result is in kilowatts (kW) if Torque (T) is input in Newton-meters (Nm) and Speed (N) is in RPM.

key_concepts.explanation: A geometric property of a cross-section that dictates its resistance to torsional deformation. For a solid circular shaft, J = (pi * D^4) / 32.

sections.title: Principal Stresses and Mohr's Circle
sections.description: Analytical and graphical methods for determining the maximum normal stresses and maximum shear stresses acting on inclined planes in complex 2D stress systems.

key_concepts.explanation: Specific, mutually perpendicular planes within a stressed body upon which the resultant shear stress is absolutely zero (tau = 0). The purely normal stresses acting on these specific planes are known as principal stresses.

A powerful graphical representation of the 2D state of stress at a point. The absolute radius of Mohr's circle is mathematically equal to the maximum in-plane shear stress (tau_max) at that specific point.

equations: Where sigma1 is the major principal stress and sigma2 is the minor principal stress.
